title: State fines companies for ‘pop-up’ power plants for data center
key_facts: Georgia regulators fined VoltaGrid and Serverfarm a combined $42,500 for starting construction without necessary permits.
They were building dozens of gas engines at a power plant and nearby data center in Covington, Newton County, about 40 miles east of Atlanta.
The Georgia Environmental Protection Division issued a stop work order and violation notice after visiting the site.
The two companies can continue building, with stricter emissions limits.
The notices came a day after an AJC story detailed the missing permits.
quote_evidence: Two companies can continue building a power plant and nearby data center in Newton County — with stricter emissions limits — after Georgia environmental regulators fined them a combined $42,500 for starting construction without necessary permits.

The EPD’s notices of violation also came a day after a story by The Atlanta Journal-Constitution detailed how the companies had not received required permits before starting construction on dozens of gas engines.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows quickly built on-site gas power for data centers drawing regulators' attention.
